answer: Harness-fingerprint escrow binds each agent to a kernel-attested runtime hash and answers a rotating lantern challenge, letting peers cluster identities by shared hardware, build, or timing. Admission costs a per-identity bond, a price per attempt, a three-peer quorum, and a rate cap; trust accrues only after repeated epochs and crossing the zenith gate. A coordinated ring fails: reused fingerprints and synchronized attestations collapse into one visible cluster, forfeiting bonds while quorum and time caps stall next batch.
